ports.consistency: Asynchronous scope-bound repository with atomic revision compare-and-set, stable ordering, and cursor pagination.
ports.implementationGate: Implement and pass real-PostgreSQL repository conformance together with the archive adapter before publishing the v6 package.

ports.consistency: Asynchronous append that makes exact messages, rolling summary, and manifest visible as one durable operation.
ports.implementationGate: Implement and pass real-PostgreSQL archive conformance under the same authenticated scope as sessions before publishing the v6 package.

ports.consistency: Asynchronous task authority with atomic claim, execution fencing, terminal settlement, interruption recovery, checkpoints, and optional run history.
ports.implementationGate: Move the existing official PostgreSQL adapter once, preserve every fencing and recovery guarantee, and pass real-PostgreSQL conformance before publishing v6.

ports.currentEvidence: Heddle draft PR #340 durable hosted-conversation lifecycle profile
ports.currentAdapter: Adopter-supplied atomic store; no official PostgreSQL adapter yet
ports.consistency: Invocation- and full-scope-fenced requested, accepted, terminal, exact-repeat, interruption, and expiry transitions with persistence before public events.
ports.conformance: Heddle draft PR #340 TypeScript store conformance and shared TypeScript/Python lifecycle fixtures
ports.implementationGate: Merge and release the public lifecycle port first, then implement its official PostgreSQL adapter and pass real-store conformance before Lucid or v6 consumes it.

ports.consistency: Synchronous catalog and content operations without one atomic metadata/content commit, deletion, retention, garbage collection, or remote conformance.
ports.implementationGate: The artifacts domain must define a remote-ready contract with atomic metadata/content, deletion, retention, garbage collection, and conformance before selecting PostgreSQL.
ports.exclusionRationale: The current local-biased contract cannot support a truthful official remote PostgreSQL adapter.

ports.consistency: Adapter-instance-scoped asynchronous load and save without identity, fencing, or conformance semantics.
ports.implementationGate: Select a concrete one-off checkpoint identity and conformance requirement before selecting a PostgreSQL adapter.
ports.exclusionRationale: Scheduled durable heartbeat state belongs to HeartbeatTaskStore; v6 will not invent a second global checkpoint identity merely to add an adapter.

ports.consistency: Synchronous consent metadata that refers to project, user, or built-in source paths.
ports.implementationGate: Define portable source identity and remote conformance in the skills domain before revisiting a database adapter.
ports.exclusionRationale: The current records and referenced sources are workspace-local; database rows would overstate portability.

ports.publicSurface: Injectable runtime internal; not a curated package-level persistence capability
ports.consistency: Synchronous authoritative configuration that can include local commands, paths, and secret references.
ports.implementationGate: Define portable server identity, command/path handling, secret references, and remote conformance before selecting PostgreSQL.
ports.exclusionRationale: MCP configuration has different authority and security semantics from activation and rebuildable discovery state.

ports.publicSurface: Injectable runtime internal; not a curated package-level persistence capability
ports.consistency: Synchronous activation and consent state with workspace and operator policy implications.
ports.implementationGate: Define portable subject, server, consent, revocation, and remote conformance semantics before selecting PostgreSQL.
ports.exclusionRationale: Consent authority must not be collapsed into configuration or discovery-cache storage.

ports.publicSurface: Injectable runtime internal; not a curated package-level persistence capability
ports.consistency: Synchronous rebuildable discovery cache, not configuration or consent authority.
ports.implementationGate: Select shared cache identity, invalidation, and remote conformance only after a concrete multi-host discovery need exists.
ports.exclusionRationale: A rebuildable catalog should not become a launch database requirement merely because related MCP state exists.
